hypothesis: The 2,896 printed LP2 word lengths carry plaintext word order at some scope (global, section, page, paragraph, sentence, line, or a local patch).
threshold: PREREG: 25 tests (12 order-inside-scope A_U [LLR, MI; within-U shuffle null], 10 composition B_U [G, SS; global null], 1 patch scan C, 2 per-unit max D), Bonferroni family 0.01 -> per-test 4.0e-4, 10,000-draw real nulls; informative iff plant power >= 0.8 (A, C) / >= 0.5 on own-scope plant with size <= 2 alpha (B, D).

control_detail.A_U (12 tests): power 1.00 on 21 intact 2,896-word English windows (7 corpora; LLR model trained on held-out halves); size 0.00 on globally shuffled plants
control_detail.solved Cicada printed lengths (739 words: A_global_LLR z=+3.79 vs bar 3.35 (scales to ~+7.5 at 2,896 words)
control_detail.C scan: 0.91 on an intact stream; patch power 0.00 (w<=100), 0.15 (200), 0.23 (400)
control_detail.B_U (10 tests): FAILED scope-discrimination criterion (power <= 0.52 on own-scope plants) -> uninformative

null: Within-scope shuffle of LP2 lengths (A), global shuffle (B, C), within-unit shuffle max (D); 10,000 draws.
result: NEGATIVE for order: all 12 A tests null (z -1.82..+0.24, p >= 0.38); C null (z_max 3.03 vs bar 4.56, p 0.30); D_sect null (p 0.29). LP2 lengths carry no plaintext-order signal at any tested scope down to the line (~5 words) at measured power 1.00 (LP2 A_global_LLR z=-1.18 vs solved-Cicada +3.79 on 739 words). The scope of any shuffle is NOT identified: English shuffled within sentence/paragraph/page/section is indistinguishable from a global shuffle by every statistic (power <= 0.05; line scope 0.48).
coverage: Adjacent-length order at 6 scopes x 2 statistics at power 1.00; composition heterogeneity at 5 scopes (uninformative); local ordered patches at power 0.23 (400 words) or less; single sections 0.65.
not_covered: Which scope the lengths were permuted within: sentence/paragraph/page/section are indistinguishable from global (power <= 0.05) because the B composition statistics fail their plants.
Ordered patches shorter than ~400 words and single ordered pages (power 0.00-0.23).
Non-adjacent (long-range or keyed-permutation) order; registers other than English GP (LLR is English-trained; MI is model-free).
reopens_if: A higher-power scope statistic (e.g. a sentence-level length-multiset model) passes a within-sentence plant; or a non-English plaintext register is evidenced and the LLR is retrained for it.
notes: Measures the Fable52 T8 design flaw instead of repeating it: composition statistics have low power on real prose, so the shuffle scope cannot be identified from lengths; reported uninformative, not negative. Solved reference = the 739 PRINTED words (Fable52 used 875 reference-text words incl. editorial insertions).

hypothesis: The printed rune order is the order in which the doublet filter ran, continuous across printed word/line/page breaks (spaces do not cut the stream into reordered pieces).
threshold: PREREG Q4: estimates only. q = fraction of printed adjacencies not adjacent at filter time, baseline = within-word residual doublet rate; Wilson 95% upper bound.

control_detail.R2 demo: ordered vs word-shuffled English under OTP+filter give identical cipher statistics (IoC*29 1.0001 vs 1.0006)

result: Lag-1 equalities 86 vs 447 expected; lags 2-10 normal (438-479). Word breaks: q_hat 0.06, 95% upper 0.20; line breaks 0.02 (upper 0.39); page breaks 0/54 (no power). At least ~80% of printed word boundaries lie inside filter-contiguous runs. No key-independent plaintext-order test exists on OTP-class ciphertext (analytic + demo).
coverage: Cipher/filter-stream order at lag 1 across word and line breaks.
not_covered: Plaintext order (untestable from ciphertext alone under an OTP-class key).
reopens_if: A non-uniform key class is evidenced (plaintext-order statistics become possible).
notes: Decoders should treat the rune stream as contiguous and ignore printed spaces.
